title: Staples Canada says customer data accessed during 'security incident' on print website
summary: Staples Canada says there was a "security incident" on its staplesprint.ca website in early November, which saw a third party get unauthorized access to certain customer data.

image.caption: Staples Canada is revealing there was a 'security incident' on its staplesprint.ca website in early November. (Doug Ives/The Canadian Press)

blocks.text: Staples Canada says there was a "security incident" on its staplesprint.ca website in early November, which saw a third party get unauthorized access to certain customer data.
Incident occurred between Nov. 1 and Nov. 5, company tells customers in email notice
A company spokesperson told CBC News via email Friday night that the incident "did not impact" any of Staples' other websites.

CBC News has viewed a copy of an email notice sent to some customers advising them that "an unknown party gained unauthorized access to our staplesprint.ca website ... and had access to certain customer personal information."
The company told customers in that notice that "no financial information was exposed" and Staples took prompt action to exclude "the threat actor from our system."

The notice also told customers that the company suspected their personal information "may have been accessed" and advised them to be vigilant about any unsolicited emails asking for personal information.
The Staples spokesperson told CBC News that the company is "taking this matter very seriously" and a full investigation is taking place, with the company assessing "the full scope of the incident."
The company did not specify to CBC News how many customers it believes may have been affected.
